statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-39831 (GO-2026-5019, GHSA-89gr-r52h-f8rx): in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, Verify for the FIDO/U2F security key types sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com and sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com did not check the User Presence flag, so signatures made without a physical touch of the key were accepted. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5019, https://go.dev/issue/79566, https://go.dev/cl/781662, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. Read every published build-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only; every download was checked against the checksum in the package index. Each package holds one program, the Go program /usr/bin/build. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the repository serves one copy, which matches one of the three checksums, and that copy was read. Every build before 2.17.3-r0 carries golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 to v0.51.0 (2.17.1-r0 has v0.51.0); 2.17.3-r0 and every later build carry v0.52.0 or later, and the current 2.29.1-r1 has v0.59.0. Checked against the function names recorded in the Go function table (pclntab), /usr/bin/build contains vulnerable functions the advisory names, golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.Dial, NewClientConn, (*Certificate).Verify, (*skECDSAPublicKey).Verify and (*skEd25519PublicKey).Verify, in every build. So the builds before 2.17.3-r0 are affected and the range ends at 2.17.3-r0.

This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, x86_64 and aarch64), together with the doc and oci-config subpackages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Alpine security repository for Alpine 3.23 hold only an image configuration YAML file and no program. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39831 (GO-2026-5019): The Verify() method for FIDO/U2F security key types (sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com, sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com) did not check the User Presence flag. Signatures generated without physical touch were accepted, allowing unattended use of a hardware security key. To restore the previous behavior, return a "no-touch-required" extension in Permissions.Extensions from PublicKeyCallback. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5019, https://go.dev/issue/79566, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI, https://go.dev/cl/781662). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Debian security repository for Debian 13 hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog, and no program. The same byte search of the same files finds the string golang.org/x/net/html, an example import path in the help text of go list, in the go command of every published golang-1.26 and golang-1.26-dev package, so the search works on these files. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
